tasks.title: Stored roles, policy and durable team foundations preserve secure sign-in
tasks.spec: ## Repository: console, Prerequisite check; Required behavior 1-2 (unchanged 27-row matrix, named actions and target policy), 3 (live stored roles and policy-derived Overview requiredRole), 5 (extend the existing single predicate and both callers), 6-7 (migration 3 and append-only People event foundation), 17 (verified-hash session creation), 19 (link primitives). Acceptance 1, 2 row 1, 3 for existing routes, 8 append-only/restart foundation, 10; Documentation for these changes. Before editing, verify the merged #563/#718 prerequisites and migration number; apply the spec's reuse/hold rule if a scoped feature already exists. Create the team-store factory and wire the required teamStore dependency in main.ts and every existing test constructor now; add each transactional operation with its complete flow in later tasks. Build the four-role fixture with real stored roles, enrolled Owner/Admin and no roleOf override. Sign-in's atomic hash revalidation belongs here, before removal or reset can race it; test a gated verifier against a changed hash or deleted user directly, then exercise the real flows in T3/T4. Preserve the dispatcher, shell, TOTP machinery, existing expected values except the explicitly specified changes, dependency pins and tooling gates. Every task must leave lint, typecheck and the full suite green.

tasks.spec: ## Repository: console; Required behavior 3 (public invite order, anonymous CSRF, a: tokens, replay precedence and successful session rotation), 8-10 (Team listing, pending invitations, creation/revocation/acceptance as one lifecycle), 19 and 21 (origins, rendering, labels and safe logs). Acceptance 2 rows 14-15 and team.view, 3 for these routes, 4, 4a invite cases, 4b invite cases, 6 invited Admin, 8 invite events/rollback, 11 HTTP page checks; corresponding Counterexamples, Security impact and Documentation. Team becomes available through #718 navigation and protected routes; reuse shared states and confirmations and use s: tokens on protected POSTs. Complete the Team listing and invitation forms here; later tasks add their own action links and forms alongside their handlers. Invites are copied by hand, never emailed; every mutation rechecks authority and writes its People event in the same transaction. Preserve #563's invited-Admin enrolment gate and new full-session cookie after confirmation.

acceptance.expected: 0 fail; anonymous GET issues CSRF cookie and a: form token, valid POST gives 303, missing/mismatched anonymous CSRF or foreign Origin gives 403 without mutation. Invalid GET sets no cookie. Existing Admin session rotation leaves 0 rows for its digest and exactly 1 new Member session; unknown session cookie also succeeds. Invited Admin gets 303 /account/authenticator and cannot GET /team until enrolment creates a full cookie, then 200. Invite event insert failure gives 500 and rolls back; no secrets in logs/metrics/People rows, CSP unchanged, no script on link pages, csrf immediately precedes form_token.

tasks.title: Team changes enforce target authority, confirmations and session invalidation
tasks.spec: ## Repository: console; Required behavior 2-5 (target/commit checks, fixed-text forbidden states and Owner-only organisation 2FA switch), 8-9 (per-person action links), 12-15 (2FA reset, role changes, removal and transfer), 20 (API-token disclosure), 21. Acceptance 2 rows 16-19, 23-25 and team.require-2fa, 3 for these routes, 5a sign-in versus removal, 6 promotion/switch/2FA reset, 7, 8 role/removal events and forced rollback, 11 HTTP page checks; all associated Counterexamples, Security impact and Documentation. Reuse #718 typed/plain confirmation helpers and revision field; target checks follow dispatcher role/form-token checks and repeat inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Only Owner changes any role; nobody targets Owner; an Admin acts only on Member/Viewer. Every role change deletes all target sessions; transfer to an enrolled Admin demotes the former Owner and deletes both people's sessions. Removal retains People identity/history and explicitly warns that API tokens stay valid. Verify authority invalidation of existing invites after issuer demotion/removal/transfer. The Team page uses links for per-person actions and only its bounded top-level forms.

acceptance.command: bun test src/server.team.test.ts src/server.roles.test.ts src/states.test.ts src/team-store.test.ts
acceptance.expected: 0 fail; implemented matrix rows have the literal allowed/denied statuses in acceptance 2 and denied mutations change 0 rows and make 0 fake-api requests. Owner targets give 403 'No one can change the owner account in the console.'; Member/Viewer transfer targets give 403 'Only an admin can become the owner.'; existing role-denial rendering stays byte-identical. Wrong typed name gives 422, stale/reused-id revision 409, transfer without authenticator 409. Transfer gives 303 /sign-in?transfer=done, exactly 1 Owner, former Owner Admin and 0 sessions for either. Removal cascades sessions/factors/reset links while retaining event identity; failed People insertion rolls role change/removal back with 500. Focused coverage is not an exit-0 requirement.

A live Viewer session gives 303 /account/authenticator with the switch on and 200 on Overview with it off. Administrative 2FA reset leaves 0 authenticators/recovery_codes/sessions of the target and follows acceptance 6 next-sign-in rules. Held sign-in versus actual removal gives 401 with 0 new sessions. Issuer authority loss makes existing invites 404; stale actor at commit gives 403 with 0 mutations/events. A 60-person Team retains working form tokens within the 100-token budget. Each successful action adds exactly 1 specified People row; no secret-bearing logs or labels.

tasks.title: Password links and own changes commit once without stale credential writes
tasks.spec: ## Repository: console; Required behavior 3 (public reset order and replay precedence), 8-9 (reset issuance confirmation and link), 11 (team reset lifecycle), 16-17 (own password compare-and-set and complete deterministic credential-race coverage), 19, 21. Acceptance 2 rows 20-22 and 27, 3 completed production route table, 4a reset cases including in-flight replay, 4b reset with foreign session cookie, 5, 5a, 8 password/reset People events, 11 HTTP page checks, 12 real main.ts wiring; corresponding Counterexamples, Security impact and Documentation. Reuse anonymous a: tokens on reset forms and #563 recheckPassword/deleteOtherSessions semantics on the own-password route; form-token checks precede hashing at the specified point. Reset issuance does not sign out; successful use revalidates link/issuer/target, ends all target sessions, keeps factors/recovery codes and starts no session. Public routes do not inspect a session cookie except T2's post-commit invite rotation. Complete sign-in/reset/removal and own-change race tests with gated verifier/hash fakes, never timers. The reset commit accepts owner-recovery kind according to section 11 when added by T5; no web Owner-reset permission is introduced here.

acceptance.expected: 0 fail; Admin Member/Viewer reset issuance 200, Member denial 403, Owner Admin issuance 200 and Admin denial 403, Owner-target reset 403; all four roles own-password 303 and anonymous request 303 /sign-in?next=%2Faccount%2Fpassword. Reset works at +86399999 and gives 404 at +86400000 or after successful use; replacement, removed target, changed target role or lost issuer authority invalidates old links. Successful reset gives 303 /sign-in?reset=done, 0 target sessions, preserves authenticator/recovery rows, old password fails and new password reaches /sign-in/factor. Own change keeps its current session, deletes other sessions and emits exactly 1 user.password-change; sixth current-password attempt after five failures gives 429 and 129-code-point password gives 422. Focused coverage is not an exit-0 requirement.

acceptance.command: bun test src/server.races.test.ts src/server.sign-in.test.ts src/server.reset.test.ts src/server.security.test.ts

Own change held at verification or hash versus reset gives 409 with the section 16 text, reset fake hash remains, 1 user.password-reset and 0 user.password-change events. Two own changes give 303 then 409; role change during own change gives 409 with hash unchanged; reset held before own change still commits last with 303 and its fake hash stored. Anonymous CSRF failures give 403 without mutations; successful reset replay gives 404 and no form-token-refusal log, in-flight same-token replay gives 409 Already submitted linking to /sign-in and first request later 303. Foreign user's cookie is untouched by reset. Digest/secret scans find 0 leaks, raw malformed paths give 404 with label other, and forms keep the required field order and CSP.
